variants.context: Edge ML deployment means running a trained model inside or near the product that uses its prediction: a phone, camera, vehicle computer, industrial gateway, or microcontroller. The device can respond without a cloud round trip, keep sensitive inputs local, and continue through a network outage.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Treat the device as a measured contract”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Freeze the contract
pairs.detail: Name supported cohorts, task-quality floors, latency deadlines, resource ceilings, fallback behavior, and release owners.
pairs.explanation: Name supported cohorts, task-quality floors, latency deadlines, resource ceilings, fallback behavior, and release owners.

pairs.label: Export and inspect
pairs.detail: Convert the model, validate signatures and operators, sign the bundle, and bind it to compatible runtime versions.
pairs.explanation: Convert the model, validate signatures and operators, sign the bundle, and bind it to compatible runtime versions.

pairs.label: Profile the real path
pairs.detail: Measure load, preprocessing, warm inference, postprocessing, peak memory, energy, heat, and task quality on representative devices.
pairs.explanation: Measure load, preprocessing, warm inference, postprocessing, peak memory, energy, heat, and task quality on representative devices.

pairs.label: Release by cohort
pairs.detail: Canary the exact bundle, enforce independent gates, retain the known-good version, and stop promotion automatically on failure.
pairs.explanation: Canary the exact bundle, enforce independent gates, retain the known-good version, and stop promotion automatically on failure.

pairs.label: Operate offline
pairs.detail: Keep inference and rollback bounded without connectivity; queue versioned telemetry and reconcile it when the network returns.
pairs.explanation: Keep inference and rollback bounded without connectivity; queue versioned telemetry and reconcile it when the network returns.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Choose a runtime after proving the execution path”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: LiteRT
pairs.detail: Google's on-device runtime supports converted models across CPU, GPU, and NPU backends.
pairs.explanation: Google's on-device runtime supports converted models across CPU, GPU, and NPU backends. Inspect supported operators and benchmark the exact CompiledModel or interpreter path on target devices.

pairs.label: ONNX Runtime Mobile
pairs.detail: Start with a complete runtime while validating the model, then consider a reduced operator build.
pairs.explanation: Start with a complete runtime while validating the model, then consider a reduced operator build. Check execution-provider partitioning because unsupported operators can push graph regions onto a slower fallback.

pairs.label: Core ML
pairs.detail: Core ML can use the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine.
pairs.explanation: Core ML can use the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine. Treat compute-unit selection and model specialization as device-specific behavior and profile the integrated application.

pairs.label: TensorRT
pairs.detail: TensorRT compiles a graph into an engine for NVIDIA hardware.
pairs.explanation: TensorRT compiles a graph into an engine for NVIDIA hardware. Serialized engines are not portable across platforms by default, and untrusted engines must be treated like untrusted executable code.

ONNX Runtime Mobile: Start with a complete runtime while validating the model, then consider a reduced operator build. Core ML: Core ML can use the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine. TensorRT: TensorRT compiles a graph into an engine for NVIDIA hardware.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Optimize against evidence, not a compression promise”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Quantize
pairs.detail: Map weights and possibly activations to lower-precision types.
pairs.explanation: Map weights and possibly activations to lower-precision types. Use representative calibration data when required, verify operator support, and test quality by important slice.

pairs.label: Change the graph
pairs.detail: Replace unsupported or expensive operations, reduce input resolution, use a mobile-oriented architecture, or distill into a smaller student.
pairs.explanation: Replace unsupported or expensive operations, reduce input resolution, use a mobile-oriented architecture, or distill into a smaller student. Re-train and re-evaluate the task contract.

pairs.label: Reduce the runtime
pairs.detail: Ship only required operators when the runtime supports a reduced build.
pairs.explanation: Ship only required operators when the runtime supports a reduced build. Measure the final application package rather than quoting the model artifact alone.

pairs.label: Tune the pipeline
pairs.detail: Reuse buffers, bound concurrency, avoid input copies, warm expected paths, and profile preprocessing plus postprocessing.
pairs.explanation: Reuse buffers, bound concurrency, avoid input copies, warm expected paths, and profile preprocessing plus postprocessing. Model invocation is only one part of latency.
